title: Laboratory Safety & Management
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian polytechnic/university 100L Laboratory Safety & Management curriculum: hazard classification, personal protective equipment, safety data sheets, chemical storage/segregation, fire safety and extinguisher classes, spill response, waste disposal, first aid, biohazards, safety signage, and basic laboratory stock/record management.

questions.question: What does the acronym 'SDS' stand for in laboratory safety practice?
options: Standard Data Sheet
Safety Data Sheet
Solvent Disposal System
Sample Documentation Summary
questions.correct_answer: Safety Data Sheet
questions.explanation: SDS stands for Safety Data Sheet, a document providing information on the properties, hazards, handling, storage, and emergency measures for a chemical substance.

questions.question: Which piece of personal protective equipment (PPE) is essential for protecting the eyes during general laboratory work?
options: Lab coat
Safety goggles
Nitrile gloves
Closed shoes
questions.correct_answer: Safety goggles
questions.explanation: Safety goggles protect the eyes from splashes, fumes, and flying particles, which lab coats, gloves, and shoes do not.

questions.question: Why should open-toed sandals never be worn in a science laboratory?
options: They are considered unfashionable
They leave the feet exposed to spilled chemicals, broken glass, or dropped heavy/hot objects
They are more expensive than closed shoes
There is no real safety reason; it is only a dress code preference
questions.correct_answer: They leave the feet exposed to spilled chemicals, broken glass, or dropped heavy/hot objects
questions.explanation: Closed, non-slip footwear protects the feet from chemical spills, glass shards, and falling objects, all common laboratory hazards.

questions.question: Which class of fire extinguisher is appropriate for extinguishing fires involving flammable liquids such as solvents?
options: Class A
Class B
Class C
Class D
questions.correct_answer: Class B
questions.explanation: Class B extinguishers are designed for fires involving flammable liquids and gases; Class A is for ordinary combustibles like paper and wood.

questions.question: A Class D fire extinguisher is specifically designed for fires involving:
options: Ordinary combustibles like paper
Flammable liquids
Combustible metals such as magnesium or sodium
Electrical equipment
questions.correct_answer: Combustible metals such as magnesium or sodium
questions.explanation: Class D extinguishers use special dry powder agents formulated to suppress fires involving reactive combustible metals, which water or foam can worsen.

questions.question: Why should water never be used to extinguish an electrical fire?
options: Water is too expensive to use in emergencies
Water conducts electricity and can cause electric shock to the person using it
Water evaporates too quickly to be effective
Water makes the fire smell worse
questions.correct_answer: Water conducts electricity and can cause electric shock to the person using it
questions.explanation: Water is an electrical conductor, so using it on a live electrical fire risks electrocuting the person attempting to extinguish it; a CO2 or dry powder extinguisher should be used instead.

questions.question: In chemical storage, why must oxidizing agents (e.g. potassium permanganate) be stored separately from flammable/combustible materials?
options: To save shelf space
Because oxidizers can intensify a fire or cause spontaneous combustion when in contact with flammable materials
Because they have different colors and look untidy together
There is no real safety reason for this practice
questions.correct_answer: Because oxidizers can intensify a fire or cause spontaneous combustion when in contact with flammable materials
questions.explanation: Oxidizing agents readily supply oxygen to support combustion, so storing them near flammables greatly increases fire risk.

questions.question: Concentrated acids and concentrated bases should generally be stored:
options: Together in the same cabinet for convenience
Separately, in dedicated corrosive-resistant cabinets, to prevent violent reaction if containers leak
In the same container to save space
Next to flammable solvents
questions.correct_answer: Separately, in dedicated corrosive-resistant cabinets, to prevent violent reaction if containers leak
questions.explanation: Storing strong acids and bases apart in corrosion-resistant cabinets prevents a dangerous, potentially violent neutralization reaction if leakage or breakage occurs.

questions.question: What is the correct emergency procedure when a chemical splashes into a person's eyes in the laboratory?
options: Rub the eyes vigorously to remove the chemical
Immediately flush the eyes with copious running water at an eyewash station for at least 15 minutes
Apply a dry bandage and wait for symptoms to pass
Close the eyes tightly and apply pressure
questions.correct_answer: Immediately flush the eyes with copious running water at an eyewash station for at least 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Prolonged flushing with running water dilutes and removes the chemical, minimizing tissue damage; rubbing or delaying treatment worsens injury.

questions.question: What is the first general step to take when a small chemical spill occurs on a laboratory bench?
options: Ignore it and continue working
Alert others nearby, assess the hazard, and contain/clean it using the appropriate spill kit and PPE
Immediately leave the building without informing anyone
Wipe it with bare hands and a paper towel
questions.correct_answer: Alert others nearby, assess the hazard, and contain/clean it using the appropriate spill kit and PPE
questions.explanation: Proper spill response starts with alerting others and assessing the hazard before containing and cleaning the spill with suitable protective equipment, preventing exposure or spread.

questions.question: Biohazardous waste (e.g. used culture plates, contaminated swabs) should be disposed of by:
options: Placing it in the regular household trash
Autoclaving or otherwise decontaminating it before disposal in designated biohazard containers
Pouring it down the sink
Burning it in the open laboratory
questions.correct_answer: Autoclaving or otherwise decontaminating it before disposal in designated biohazard containers
questions.explanation: Biohazardous materials must be rendered non-infectious (typically by autoclaving) and disposed of in labeled biohazard containers to prevent spread of infection.

questions.question: Which color is internationally used on biohazard waste bags/bins to signify infectious or biological waste?
options: Blue
Yellow/red (biohazard-labeled)
Green
White
questions.correct_answer: Yellow/red (biohazard-labeled)
questions.explanation: Biohazardous waste containers are typically yellow or red and marked with the universal biohazard symbol to distinguish them from general waste.

questions.question: Why must chemical waste never be poured directly down the laboratory sink without proper procedure?
options: It may block the sink pipes permanently
It can contaminate the water system, react dangerously with other waste, or violate environmental disposal regulations
It wastes valuable chemicals
It has no real consequence if done occasionally
questions.correct_answer: It can contaminate the water system, react dangerously with other waste, or violate environmental disposal regulations
questions.explanation: Improper disposal of chemical waste can pollute water systems, cause hazardous reactions with other substances in the drain, and breach environmental safety regulations.

questions.question: What does the hazard pictogram showing a flame typically indicate on a chemical container?
options: The substance is corrosive
The substance is flammable
The substance is an irritant only
The substance is environmentally hazardous
questions.correct_answer: The substance is flammable
questions.explanation: The flame pictogram (GHS hazard symbol) warns that a substance is flammable and can easily ignite.

questions.question: What does the corrosion (test tubes pouring liquid onto a hand/surface) pictogram indicate?
options: The substance is explosive
The substance can cause severe skin burns, eye damage, or corrode metals
The substance is radioactive
The substance is a simple irritant with no real danger
questions.correct_answer: The substance can cause severe skin burns, eye damage, or corrode metals
questions.explanation: The GHS corrosion pictogram warns of substances that can severely damage living tissue or corrode metal on contact, such as strong acids and bases.

questions.question: What is the correct action if a fire alarm sounds while working with an active experiment in the lab?
options: Continue the experiment until it is complete
Safely stop/secure the experiment if possible, then evacuate immediately via the nearest exit
Hide under the laboratory bench
Use the lift/elevator to leave quickly
questions.correct_answer: Safely stop/secure the experiment if possible, then evacuate immediately via the nearest exit
questions.explanation: Standard fire evacuation procedure requires safely securing hazardous work if time allows, then evacuating via stairs (never lifts) to the nearest exit and assembly point.

questions.question: Why is eating or drinking strictly prohibited inside a working laboratory?
options: It is only a matter of institutional etiquette
It risks accidental ingestion of chemical or biological contaminants
Food attracts insects that damage equipment
There is no scientific reason; it is purely a rule for tidiness
questions.correct_answer: It risks accidental ingestion of chemical or biological contaminants
questions.explanation: Food and drink can become contaminated by chemicals, reagents, or biological agents present in the laboratory, posing a serious risk of accidental poisoning or infection.

questions.question: What is the correct use of a fume hood (fume cupboard) in the laboratory?
options: As additional bench space for general storage
To safely contain and vent toxic, volatile, or noxious fumes away from the laboratory worker
To increase the temperature of reactions
To store PPE such as gloves and goggles
questions.correct_answer: To safely contain and vent toxic, volatile, or noxious fumes away from the laboratory worker
questions.explanation: A fume hood draws air through a controlled opening, containing and exhausting hazardous vapours or gases to protect the worker from inhalation exposure.

questions.question: Which type of gloves is generally recommended for handling most laboratory chemicals due to good chemical resistance?
options: Cotton gloves
Nitrile gloves
Leather work gloves
Wool gloves
questions.correct_answer: Nitrile gloves
questions.explanation: Nitrile gloves offer good resistance to a wide range of chemicals and are commonly used in laboratories, unlike cotton, leather, or wool which absorb chemicals or offer no real barrier.

questions.question: What immediate first aid step should be taken for a minor thermal burn from a hot apparatus (e.g. a hot crucible)?
options: Apply ice directly to the burn
Cool the burn under cool running water for several minutes
Apply butter or oil to the burn
Pop any blisters that form immediately
questions.correct_answer: Cool the burn under cool running water for several minutes
questions.explanation: Cooling a burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water reduces tissue damage; ice, oils, or butter can worsen injury or cause infection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Material Safety Data Sheet's 'section on handling and storage'?
options: To list the manufacturer's marketing information
To describe safe handling precautions and appropriate storage conditions for the chemical
To provide the retail price of the chemical
To list unrelated laboratory equipment
questions.correct_answer: To describe safe handling precautions and appropriate storage conditions for the chemical
questions.explanation: The handling and storage section of an SDS gives specific precautions for safe use and the correct conditions (temperature, compatibility, ventilation) for storing the chemical.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines 'acute toxicity' as a hazard classification?
options: Harm that develops only after many years of exposure
Adverse health effects occurring after a single or short-term exposure to a substance
A substance that is harmless in any quantity
A hazard that only affects laboratory equipment, not people
questions.correct_answer: Adverse health effects occurring after a single or short-term exposure to a substance
questions.explanation: Acute toxicity refers to harmful effects that appear soon after a single or brief exposure, as opposed to chronic toxicity which develops from long-term exposure.

questions.question: Why should long hair be tied back and loose jewelry removed before laboratory work?
options: To follow a purely aesthetic dress code
To prevent them from catching fire, being contaminated, or getting caught in equipment
Because loose hair slows down experiments
There is no safety reason; it is a matter of personal choice only
questions.correct_answer: To prevent them from catching fire, being contaminated, or getting caught in equipment
questions.explanation: Loose hair and jewelry can catch fire near open flames, become contaminated with chemicals, or get caught in moving equipment such as centrifuges.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of maintaining a chemical inventory register in a laboratory?
options: To track quantities, locations, and expiry dates of chemicals for safety and reordering purposes
To record student attendance
To replace the need for safety training
To list only the most expensive chemicals
questions.correct_answer: To track quantities, locations, and expiry dates of chemicals for safety and reordering purposes
questions.explanation: A chemical inventory helps the laboratory track stock levels, storage locations, and expiry dates, supporting both safety compliance and efficient reordering.

questions.question: What does 'incompatible chemicals' mean in the context of laboratory storage?
options: Chemicals that are simply expensive to store together
Chemicals that can react dangerously (e.g. explode, ignite, release toxic gas) if mixed or stored close together
Chemicals of different colors
Chemicals produced by different manufacturers
questions.correct_answer: Chemicals that can react dangerously (e.g. explode, ignite, release toxic gas) if mixed or stored close together
questions.explanation: Incompatible chemicals can undergo hazardous reactions such as fire, explosion, or toxic gas release when combined, so they must be segregated in storage.

questions.question: What is the correct action after accidentally inhaling a small amount of toxic fume in the laboratory?
options: Continue working and ignore it if it is not severe
Move immediately to fresh air and seek medical attention if symptoms persist
Hold your breath and wait indoors
Drink large amounts of water only
questions.correct_answer: Move immediately to fresh air and seek medical attention if symptoms persist
questions.explanation: Moving to fresh air reduces further exposure, and medical evaluation ensures any respiratory harm is properly assessed and treated.

questions.question: Why is it important to label all laboratory reagent containers clearly with name, concentration, and date prepared?
options: It is only required for containers leaving the building
To prevent misuse, ensure correct handling, and track reagent stability/expiry
Because unlabeled containers are illegal to manufacture
Labels serve no functional purpose in the lab
questions.correct_answer: To prevent misuse, ensure correct handling, and track reagent stability/expiry
questions.explanation: Clear labeling prevents accidental misuse of chemicals, ensures they are handled and stored correctly, and allows tracking of how long a prepared reagent remains valid.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) in a laboratory?
options: To provide a step-by-step, standardized method for performing a task safely and consistently
To replace the need for any staff training
To serve only as a legal document with no practical use
To list the personal opinions of the laboratory head
questions.correct_answer: To provide a step-by-step, standardized method for performing a task safely and consistently
questions.explanation: An SOP documents the standardized, approved way to carry out a specific procedure, promoting safety, consistency, and quality across repeated uses.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is an example of good laboratory housekeeping practice?
options: Leaving chemical spills to be cleaned at the end of the week
Keeping aisles, walkways, and emergency exits clear of clutter and equipment
Storing personal bags and food on the laboratory bench
Leaving used glassware unwashed on the bench overnight
questions.correct_answer: Keeping aisles, walkways, and emergency exits clear of clutter and equipment
questions.explanation: Good housekeeping keeps emergency routes accessible and reduces trip hazards, spills, and contamination risks in the laboratory.
